clue.text: They're drained — a sign of a good night?

definitions.text: They're drained — a sign of a good night?

parts.words: They're drained — a sign of a good night?
parts.note: bottles drunk dry pile up by the door after a lively evening

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the bottles left lined up after a party: drained of their contents, they are evidence the night went well.
explanation.definitionFit: Empties is the everyday noun for bottles or glasses that have been finished off.

clue.text: Land English dog in trouble? On the contrary!

indicators.note: inclusion signal, reversed by what follows
the stated inclusion is flipped: trouble goes in the dog, not the dog in trouble

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
ado is fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: An English dog in a bit of bother abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary!' tells the solver to do the opposite of what the clue says: the trouble goes in the dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecuador is a South American nation, a land on the equator.

clue.text: Apply fixed rate, entering PIN

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside PIN

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: fixed here means doctored or rigged, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Instructions to apply a set rate when the card PIN is keyed in.
explanation.walkthrough: PIN is taken as written, capitals and all, so it is the container rather than a definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To pertain is to be relevant, as in rules that apply to a case.

clue.text: Writer Murdoch hailing originally from Dublin?

parts.note: Iris Murdoch, the Dublin-born novelist of The Sea, The Sea

indicators.note: the word's origin is its opening letter

parts.note: its first letter is H

explanation.surface: Asking whether novelist Iris Murdoch was born in Dublin.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: Dublin-born people are only one kind of Irish. Murdoch was in fact born in Dublin.
explanation.definitionFit: Dublin is the capital of Ireland, so someone born there is Irish.

clue.text: Tireless working to retain current doctor?

indicators.note: the shuffled letters hold the current symbol inside
working letters are put to use in a new arrangement

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A tireless doctor still at work, keeping up with current practice.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor is the verb here, as when a vet doctors a cat: neuters it.
explanation.definitionFit: To doctor an animal is to neuter it, which sterilising does.

clue.text: Gruesome barber occasionally going into club

indicators.note: the picked letters are placed inside the club word

parts.note: a mace is a heavy club used as a weapon

indicators.note: taking only some letters of barber, every other one, is using it now and then

explanation.surface: A barber who sometimes turns up at a club is described as gruesome.
explanation.definitionFit: Macabre describes things that dwell on death and horror, a close synonym of ghastly.

clue.text: Month in advance

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the third month of the year
second meaning: to walk forward in step, as troops do

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests something a month ahead; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names the spring month and also the verb for soldiers moving forward in formation.

clue.text: Wacky baccy free in online coffee shop

indicators.note: wacky means crazy, so the following letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A café where wacky tobacco is free, with internet access.
explanation.walkthrough: Baccy is British slang for tobacco.
explanation.definitionFit: A cybercafe is a café offering internet terminals to customers.

clue.text: Fought, shed blood, receiving little attention

indicators.note: the bleeding word takes the short form inside it

parts.note: to shed blood is to bleed, so bled
ATT is a short form of attention, as on a letter

explanation.surface: A soldier who fought and bled but was barely noticed.
explanation.definitionFit: Battled is a synonym of fought, as in a struggle or combat.

clue.text: Former Conservative employer's apologist?

parts.note: ex means former
an employer, one who employs something, is a user; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A former Tory employer who defends himself.
explanation.walkthrough: Employer is read as one who employs or uses something, not a boss.
explanation.definitionFit: An excuser makes excuses, offering defence or justification as an apologist does.

clue.text: Our wet weather beginning to ease in country

parts.note: for a British newspaper, 'our' country is the UK
rain is wet weather

indicators.note: only the opening letter of ease is wanted

parts.note: its first letter is E

explanation.surface: A grumble about British rain that is finally starting to let up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Our' points to the UK because the Telegraph is a British paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Ukraine is a nation in eastern Europe, so it is an example of a country.

clue.text: Old boy in tight trio constant like automaton

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step
tight means drunk, so the word trio is reeling and rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
OB is the standard abbreviation for an old boy, a former pupil
C is the symbol for a constant in mathematics and physics

explanation.surface: A former pupil squeezed into a close-knit threesome behaves mechanically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tight' is slang for drunk, which makes it an anagram signal here rather than a description of the trio.
explanation.definitionFit: Robotic means mechanical and unthinking, the way a machine-like automaton moves.

clue.text: We had this wild Freudian impulse!

indicators.note: wild letters run out of control, so the words before are scrambled

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a wild urge took hold of us.
explanation.definitionFit: Freud proposed a drive toward self-destruction, popularly called the death wish.

clue.text: Luxurious car moves along smoothly

definitions.meaning: second meaning: ... as a verb, glides on wheels

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one picture of a grand car purring along, but the two halves are separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Rolls is short for the Rolls-Royce motor, and rolls is also the verb for travelling on wheels.

clue.text: Fabulous Liverpool player in 0-0

parts.note: the figure zero is drawn as a ring
zero is also read as the letter O

explanation.surface: A legendary Liverpool footballer playing in a goalless draw.
explanation.walkthrough: Fabulous refers to the Fab Four: Ringo Starr was the Beatles' drummer, a Liverpool player of drums rather than football.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringo Starr played drums in the Beatles, the 'Fab Four' from Liverpool.

clue.text: Informed about article with book complete

parts.note: on means concerning or about
the is the definite article
all means whole or complete

explanation.surface: Someone well-read about an article with the full book.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the ball means alert and well up on things, so well-informed.

clue.text: Just one left with Cinderella running in National

indicators.note: Cinderella has two Ls; leaving only one means one is taken out
the letters of Cinderella run about into a new order

explanation.surface: Cinderella fleeing a ball, with just one slipper left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop one L from CINDERELLA so just one is left, then rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: An Icelander is a citizen of Iceland, and a national is a citizen of a country.

clue.text: Transported via Gate Four?

parts.note: a gate is an entrance
D is the fourth letter, as gates are labelled A, B, C, D

explanation.surface: Taken away through gate number four.
explanation.walkthrough: Transported means enraptured, not carried; Gate Four becomes 'Entrance D'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be entranced is to be enchanted, carried away with delight.

clue.text: Explosive material about creativity is sincere

indicators.note: the explosive and material wrap around the creativity word

parts.note: HE stands for high explosive
felt is a pressed fabric
art is creative skill

explanation.surface: Explosive stuff surrounding artistic flair is somehow genuine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Explosive material' reads as one phrase, but it splits into two pieces that go around the creativity.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartfelt feelings come from the heart, so they are deeply genuine.

clue.text: Worker catching a disease — is this going round Panama?

indicators.note: the worker takes the disease inside

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker
TB, tuberculosis, is a disease

explanation.surface: A worker falls ill, with a joke about it spreading around Panama.
explanation.walkthrough: Panama is the straw hat, not the country or canal.
explanation.definitionFit: A hatband is the ribbon encircling the crown of a hat such as a Panama.

clue.text: Road train covering miles for speedy delivery

parts.note: the A1 is Britain's longest road, written AI

indicators.note: the train word wraps round the miles letter

parts.note: rail stands for train travel

explanation.surface: Road and rail covering long distances for fast post.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is the main road from London to Edinburgh; crosswords write it AI.
explanation.definitionFit: Airmail is post carried by plane, faster than surface mail.

clue.text: Senior worker joining's first to leave!

indicators.note: the opening letter of the worker is removed

parts.note: a welder is a worker who joins metal

explanation.surface: A senior staff member whose first act is to quit.
explanation.walkthrough: A welder's job is joining metal; take off W to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An elder is an older person, so senior in age or standing.

clue.text: Follow left-winger in gentle run

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them
a Trot is a Trotskyist, a hard-left activist

explanation.surface: Tailing a socialist on a gentle jog.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogtrot is a slow, easy trotting pace, like a jog.

clue.text: Author Arthur published a little

parts.note: a paper ran a story when it published it
some means a small amount

explanation.surface: A writer called Arthur who got only a little into print.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur Ransome wrote Swallows and Amazons.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Ransome was the English writer of the Swallows and Amazons children's books.

clue.text: Reportedly given lessons making cake

indicators.note: a report is heard, so the word is said aloud

parts.note: someone given lessons has been taught

explanation.surface: A cookery course that ends in baking a cake.
explanation.walkthrough: In a British accent, with the R silent, taught and torte sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A torte is a rich, layered continental gateau.

clue.text: 1970s rock genre with keyboard in county once

parts.note: glam rock, the glitter-heavy style of Bowie and Bolan
an organ is a keyboard instrument

explanation.surface: A seventies glam band adding a keyboard player.
explanation.walkthrough: Glamorgan was a Welsh county until local-government reorganisation in 1974.
explanation.definitionFit: Glamorgan was a historic Welsh shire, abolished as an administrative area in 1974.

clue.text: Visual representation in viewing Raphael

indicators.note: the answer lies within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A visual image to be seen when looking at a Raphael painting.
explanation.definitionFit: A graph is a chart or diagram that shows data pictorially.

clue.text: Drink and drug in round tin

parts.note: O is round in shape

indicators.note: the drug letter is placed inside the tin

parts.note: a can is a tin
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Drinks and drugs stashed in a round tin.
explanation.walkthrough: The drink is slang for the sea, not a beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: The drink is informal British slang for the sea, and an ocean is a sea.

clue.text: Nursed by a Tibetan priest, sailor in state

indicators.note: the sailor is cradled inside the priest

parts.note: a lama is a Buddhist monk in Tibet
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman cared for by a Tibetan monk somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabama is one of the fifty American states, in the Deep South.

clue.text: Farewell in church always one associated with love

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever
I is the Roman numeral one
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A goodbye in church to someone always linked with love.
explanation.walkthrough: Love means nil in tennis scoring, written as O.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheerio is an informal British way of saying goodbye.

clue.text: Temptress greeted making comeback around Lima

indicators.note: the backwards word goes round the Lima letter
the word is read in the opposite direction, coming back

parts.note: hailed means greeted
Lima is L in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A seductress welcomed back on her return from Peru's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Lima looks like the Peruvian capital; it is the radio-alphabet word for L.
explanation.definitionFit: Delilah seduced Samson in the Bible, so her name stands for any seductive woman.

clue.text: Empty table seen after noon in fast food place

indicators.note: the emptied table comes after the rest
the noon letter goes inside the fast word

parts.note: to diet is to fast or cut down on food

indicators.note: emptying a word takes out its middle, leaving its outer letters

parts.note: its first and last letters are TE

explanation.surface: A bare table seen at lunchtime in a fast-food joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast food' looks like one phrase, but fast is the wordplay and food place the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinette is a small dining area or alcove, a place for eating meals.
